comments.text:
re: Kid's skincare.

I have an 8 year old daughter. I'm 44.

I am not, and have never been, a very "girly" girl. I'm not likely to ever get that way. My face? Sandpaper. I have the cheapest hand lotion ever on my desk (I literally bought it at Big Lots) and it gets used in the winter when my hands hurt.

My daughter is much more "girly". I do not mind if she wants to do things like skincare and makeup. Her grandmother is one of the people who has been able to help her here. If my kid wanted some of those Rini products, based on what I have seen as far as the ingredients go? I'm fine with it. Trying to find anything for kids who want to have a little self-care routine is so difficult.

One of my nephews was gifted bodywash for Christmas a few years ago, and his skin was way too sensitive because it was something harsh, meant for a teenager, not a kid still in single digits. I don't mind "dude" scents, found them to work REALLY well as "dude repellant" when I was living apart from my partner, so I traded him for something that he liked the smell of and wouldn't make him feel awful after a shower.

I do not see the marketing as telling kids their skin isn't perfect (which... there's issues with "perfect" being used as well, because how are they gonna feel when puberty hits and they start getting acne because hormones are a while ride). I think a kid wanting to take care of their skin, and having the options to do so, that mimics what a parent uses is not a bad thing, as long as there's also discussion of what and why.

Why does mom use this special soap for her face? Why does dad use that product in his beard? What's this hair serum grandma uses?

And a lot of parents don't want to talk to their kids that way. It's just easier to say "Oh you don't need that" and drop the discussion.

But, that's just my opinion as an Old™ person with a much younger kiddo. :V
